title: Ankara Revokes Bank Mellat License as US-Turkey Thaw Nears Erdoğan-Trump UNGA Meeting; Turkey Pitches Military Support for Saudi Under Mecca Pact
subhead: In the run-up to Erdoğan's Sept. 22 meeting with Trump in New York, Turkey revoked Iranian lender Bank Mellat's operating license and signaled it is working with Washington on 'creative ideas' to resolve the S-400 standoff, with Trump saying he will consider returning F-35s to Turkey. Separately, Ankara offered to help meet Saudi Arabia's military needs under the Mecca defense pact as Houthi attacks on the kingdom escalate.

sections.heading: US-Turkey Reset Accelerates Ahead of Erdoğan-Trump Meeting
sections.body:
Turkey's banking watchdog (BDDK) revoked the operating license of Iranian lender Bank Mellat's Istanbul branch, a decision published in the Official Gazette on Saturday, according to Al Jazeera. The regulator invoked a clause of Turkey's banking law allowing license withdrawal if continued operation risks depositors' rights or financial-system stability; the notice did not cite US measures. Bank Mellat has faced years of Western sanctions over alleged links to Iran's nuclear program, and was hit by US and Gulf sanctions in 2019 after being named among 25 entities tied to the IRGC.

The move lands days before Erdoğan is set to meet Trump in New York on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly on Sept. 22, a meeting confirmed by US envoy and Turkish officials (Daily Sabah, Türkiye Today). The context is a fast-moving reset: Trump said he will consider giving Turkey F-35 jets and that the US will lift sanctions (ABC News), while Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said Ankara is working with Washington on 'creative ideas' to solve the S-400 missile issue (Times of Israel, Arab News). The thaw follows the US Treasury's early-September sanctions on Golden Global Yatırım Bankası over alleged IRGC-Quds Force ties, which Ankara protested.
sections.whyItMatters: Revoking Bank Mellat's license is Ankara signaling alignment with the US pressure campaign on Tehran at a sensitive moment — a concrete gesture ahead of the Erdoğan-Trump summit that tests how far the long-frozen US-Turkey defense relationship can thaw toward an F-35 return and sanctions relief.

sections.heading: Turkey Pitches Military Support for Saudi Under Mecca Defense Pact
sections.body:
Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said Turkey could help meet Saudi Arabia's military needs under the Mecca defense pact, as Houthi attacks on the kingdom escalate, according to Reuters, Al Jazeera and TRT World. Turkey's foreign minister also said Türkiye plans to raise Saudi military needs with Pakistan within the alliance framework (Türkiye Today). The offer comes as Saudi forces intercepted a Houthi missile fired at Riyadh — the first air raid alert in the capital since the escalation — and as Saudi air defenses face continued drone and missile strikes linked to the wider US-Iran conflict (Al Jazeera).

The Mecca pact — which also ties in Pakistan's vowed defense of Saudi Arabia — is being stress-tested by the Houthi campaign, with analyses noting Saudi Arabia now holds defense pacts with Pakistan, Turkey, the US and others, yet the attacks continue (Indian Express, Middle East Monitor). Fidan framed institutionalizing the pact as 'game-changing' (Express Tribune).
sections.whyItMatters: Turkey is positioning itself as an active guarantor within the Mecca framework rather than a passive member, seeking strategic influence in the Gulf at a moment when Houthi strikes are testing every member's commitment — and when the US-Saudi F-35 package is drawing scrutiny.

sections.heading: Israel-Linked Investment Fraud Network Crackdown Spreads
sections.body:
Turkish authorities' operation against an alleged international investment fraud network has netted 191 detained people, including nine Israelis, according to the Jerusalem Post, the Times of Israel and i24NEWS. Turkish media and security sources describe a forex-based scheme with losses alleged in the billions of dollars (reports range from roughly $266 million up to $3 billion), with raids launched via operations coordinated across provinces (Daily Sabah, Hürriyet Daily News). Israel's foreign ministry said it is working to ensure the rights of the detained Israelis are protected (Times of Israel).

This is the latest phase of a broader regulatory crackdown that has shaken Turkey's fund industry — regulators recently froze managers and liquidated funds after the Pusula collapse triggered market stress and large outflows, with Bloomberg describing the affair as a 'ponzi-like scheme' and Daily Sabah reporting Ankara mandated large public and private banks to liquidate $18.3 billion in funds.
sections.whyItMatters: Beyond the fraud case itself, the widening enforcement drive — now with an international, Israel-linked dimension — shows Ankara tightening financial-sector controls at a moment of market fragility, while adding a sensitive foreign-policy layer to the crackdown.

sections.heading: Syria: Explosion Kills 11 Soldiers; Ankara Nears 'Final Phase' of Anti-Terror Drive
sections.body: An explosion at a Syrian military site killed 11 soldiers, with reports placing the blast in the Dayr al-Zawr area and attributing it to HTS-linked forces (Hürriyet Daily News, Al Arabiya, PressTV). Separately, President Erdoğan said Türkiye is 'nearing the final phase' of its anti-terror drive (Yeni Safak), an apparent reference to ongoing operations and the PKK-related disarmament process. Kurdish analysts continue to debate how Kurdish rights will be secured as the SDF formally dissolves in Syria (Al Jazeera), with KCK and PKK figures publicly sparring over leadership roles in the new political order (Kurdistan24, Rudaw).
sections.whyItMatters: The Deir ez-Zor blast underscores the fragility of Syria's security transition, while Erdoğan's 'final phase' language signals Ankara believes its cross-border posture and the disarmament track are converging — even as Kurdish political arrangements inside Syria remain unsettled.

sections.heading: Economy and Nuclear Track: Lira Pressure, Akkuyu Nears Launch
sections.body: Turkey's fund-market strain persisted, with the lira touching record lows amid the stock-market decline linked to the fund crisis (SuaraGarut.ID, Business Standard). On the nuclear front, Akkuyu Unit 1 reportedly entered a key pre-launch preparation stage ahead of commissioning (Türkiye Today), continuing the trajectory flagged when Erdoğan signaled a wider nuclear cooperation push with Russia — including progress on potential additional units — as the plant near the Mediterranean coast advances.
sections.whyItMatters: Financial-market stress and a nuclear project nearing first power generation frame two competing pressures on Ankara: defending the currency and funding stability amid the fund crisis, while locking in Moscow-backed energy infrastructure that also deepens dependence on Russia.

bottomLine: The defining story of the weekend is Washington-Ankara momentum: Turkey revoked Iranian Bank Mellat's license, Trump floated returning F-35s and lifting sanctions, Fidan flagged 'creative ideas' on the S-400 issue, and Erdoğan heads to New York for a Sept. 22 Trump meeting — a cluster of moves suggesting both capitals are preparing a substantive reset. Ankara's offer to back Saudi Arabia militarily under the Mecca pact shows it is also activating its Gulf and Pakistan relationships as Houthi attacks test the alliance. Running beneath these headline moves are the still-unresolved strains: the fund-market crisis and lira pressure at home, and the unsettled Kurdish political settlement in Syria. Expect the Erdoğan-Trump summit to be the pivotal test of whether the thaw translates into concrete deliverables on F-35s and sanctions relief.
